design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — warranty_claims_service task 1 (Theodore Sandoval, upstairs air-conditioning cash settlement)

0. DRAW AND SCOPE SNAPSHOT
- draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0033_national_homebuilder/warranty_claims_service/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6]}: every problem carries 6 factors.
- Occupied by task 0: warranty_ext_missed_appointment_charge + assess_missed_appointment_charge_27486c7f, warranty_ext_finish_item_settlement + accept_finish_item_cash_settlement_135d939d. Claimed here (the remainder of the charter, last task): warranty_ext_reinspection_charge (assess_reinspection_charge_a99ab20e, agent), warranty_ext_dispatch_charge (assess_emergency_dispatch_charge_91903470, agent), warranty_ext_systems_item_settlement (accept_systems_item_cash_settlement_9ecd6f20, owner=user). Union of both tasks = all 5 extended policies and all 5 task tools, pairwise disjoint.
- Choice of policies: the two remaining base charges that are 'non-warranty visits' (a re-measurement that again found a crack within tolerance; an emergency dispatch that found a homeowner-caused condition) are the natural pair whose counts feed each other's escalation; the customer-side write is the homeowner's cash acceptance on a covered systems item, which the blueprint makes the homeowner's own written decision.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
The customer asks only for cash instead of another repair on his upstairs air-conditioning item (WSR-55841-01). The systems-settlement rule says 'A systems settlement is not offered to the homeowner, and no cash-in-lieu payout is approved on it, until every emergency dispatch recorded on the coverage that the dispatch charge rules make chargeable carries its emergency dispatch charge.' The ledger shows the 2026-09-19 no-cooling dispatch (maintenance finding) uncharged. The dispatch-charge rule in turn says 'The dispatch charge is fixed only after every re-reported item that a re-measurement again found within tolerance and that the reinspection rules make chargeable carries its reinspection charge.' The ledger shows the driveway re-report WSR-55906-01 re-measured within tolerance on 2026-09-08 and uncharged. So the agent must discover a two-hop chain the customer never mentions, compute three 6-factor figures (25.20, 48.99, 886.10) in order, and hand the last write to the customer. Depth: 3 problems in a chain. Breadth: purchase community and contract price, homesite hold and its deposit ledger, five history windows (12-month reinspection and non-warranty charges, life dispatch charges, 24-month maintenance findings, coverage age), same-day covered work, response hours vs program hours, approval age vs repair target days, systems end date.

2. BASE-INVARIANT CARD
- Reinspection charge and dispatch charge (subject warranty_charge_assessed): governing base policies warranty_tolerances_and_exclusions, warranty_appointment_charges, warranty_structural_claims, warranty_transfer; no eligibility gate applies to charge assessment (the only gate, one_waiver_per_charge, applies to waivers) -> policy_scope x4 each. Superseded clauses declared in overwrite: 'An item already denied within_tolerance that is re-reported and again measured within tolerance carries reinspection_fee_usd.' (replaced by the visit-charge multiplier sentence) and 'An emergency dispatch that finds a condition caused by the homeowner or not covered carries emergency_dispatch_fee_usd.' (replaced by the scheduled-dispatch-charge sentence); the program fees (100.00, 125.00) and response hours (12) stay base parameters. Inherited: the reinspection charge only for an item already denied within tolerance and re-measured within tolerance again (WSR-55620-01 denied 2026-05-13, re-report WSR-55906-01 re-measured 2026-09-08, denied 2026-09-09); the dispatch charge only for a dispatch whose condition was homeowner-caused or not covered (maintenance_item, denied homeowner_maintenance).
- Systems settlement (subject warranty_payout_approved): warranty_payouts_and_payments ('In place of repairing a covered non-structural item, Calloway may offer a cash settlement of no more than cash_in_lieu_max_usd per claim item; it becomes a payout only when the homeowner accepts it in writing') and warranty_structural_claims -> policy_scope x2; overwrite [] (886.10 stays under the 1,000.00 ceiling). The hvac item is covered: approved 2026-06-17 under systems (36-month systems period to 2028-09-18), callback 2026-08-14 = 37 days after the 2026-07-08 repair (within 60), approved 2026-08-15.
- No time gate applies to these subjects -> temporal_feasibility [].

3. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
- Reinspection: object = the 2026-09-08 within-tolerance re-measurement of WSR-55906-01 (0.2188 in, flatwork tolerance 0.25 in). Excluded: WSR-55102-01 and WSR-55620-01 (first reports), WSR-55377-01 (re-report already charged WCH-55391). Written key: claim_item_ref WSR-55906-01.
- Dispatch: object = the 2026-09-19 dispatch to WSR-56012-01 (response 15.5 h). Only dispatch on the coverage. Written key: WSR-56012-01.
- Settlement: object = WSR-55841-01 under the latest systems approval (2026-08-15, callback_seq 1). WSR-56012-01 (also hvac) was denied, never approved. Written key: WSR-55841-01.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD
- Chain: warranty_ext_systems_item_settlement (root, on_request, owner=user) <- warranty_ext_dispatch_charge (state_due, agent) <- warranty_ext_reinspection_charge (state_due, agent).
- Edge A (root -> dispatch charge): kind state_gate, gate warranty_events.charge_type, form state. Sentence (negated direction: an offer and approval 'is not ... until' what it waits for stands): 'A systems settlement is not offered to the homeowner, and no cash-in-lieu payout is approved on it, until every emergency dispatch recorded on the coverage that the dispatch charge rules make chargeable carries its emergency dispatch charge.' Four-point test: connective 'not ... until'; waited-on side is a record-visible state (a chargeable dispatch carrying an emergency dispatch charge); no tool/id/code token; scope = every chargeable dispatch. Exactly one write brings it about: only the dispatch charge policy books emergency_dispatch_fee charges. Derivation: sentence + ledger (one dispatch, maintenance finding, no dispatch charge) + the dispatch rule -> book the dispatch charge for WSR-56012-01. False at frozen_time: dispatch row WSR-56012-01 with finding maintenance_item, only charge on the coverage is a reinspection_fee. Deletion sensitivity: skipping step 10 leaves the settlement figure at 886.10 but drops the 48.99 dispatch charge row (charges_due 25.20 instead of 74.19) — load-bearing on the terminal state as a state gate.
- Edge B (dispatch charge -> reinspection charge): kind value_input, gate nonwarranty_mult, form state. Sentence (affirmative, a charge 'is fixed only after' what it rests on): 'The dispatch charge is fixed only after every re-reported item that a re-measurement again found within tolerance and that the reinspection rules make chargeable carries its reinspection charge.' Exactly one write brings it about (only the reinspection policy books reinspection_fee charges). False at frozen_time: WSR-55906-01 within tolerance, the only reinspection charge WCH-55391 is on WSR-55377-01. Deletion sensitivity (verify.py): dispatch charge 40.83 without step 8, 48.99 with it.
- Topological order unique (chain): reinspection (step 8) -> dispatch (step 10) -> settlement (step 12). The charter now carries both directions of prerequisite sentence (task 0's 'is fixed only after', and this 'is not paid until').
- user_scenario names no charge or fee; the dispatch call, driveway crack and homesite hold are answered only if asked; tools validate nothing.

5. FACTOR CARD (handling-time world; baseline = computation document)
Reinspection charge (6): baseline 'the program's reinspection fee' = 100.00.
 borderline (param): 0.2188/0.25 = 0.875 -> 0.80 (baseline 31.50). repeat-reinspection (param): 1 charge in 12 months -> 1.25 (20.16). soil-movement (param, multi-source: category AND community, cross-difficulty purchase): flatwork + Sierra Vista Ranch -> 0.70 (36.00). settling-period (param): 12 months -> 0.90 (28.00). re-measure delay (param): 8 days -> 0.80 (31.50). shared-visit (method): one covered-work entry on 2026-09-08 (defect-confirming hvac inspection) -> half of the visit charge (whole: 50.40). Near-miss: the 2026-08-20 eleven-month walkthrough is on a different day (a walkthrough the same day would mean no charge). Result 25.20; all-baseline 100.00.
Dispatch charge (6): baseline 'the program's emergency dispatch fee' = 125.00.
 condition-class (param): no_cooling -> 0.80 (61.24). finding (param): maintenance_item -> 0.75 (65.32). non-warranty visit (param, value_input): 2 charges in 12 months incl. step 8 -> 1.50 (32.66). first-period (param, multi-source: months AND no earlier dispatch charge): 12 months, none -> 0.75 (65.32). active-buyer (param, cross-difficulty homesite + purchase): no open purchase agreement, homesite PS-0581 held with its 1,000.00 deposit received -> 0.75 (65.32); near-miss: the closed home purchase is not an open agreement. response proration (method): 15.5 h > 12 h, not > 24 h -> x 12/15.5 (whole: 63.28). Result 48.99; all-baseline 125.00.
Systems settlement (6, as reworked in round 2): baseline 'cash-in-lieu maximum x standard systems share 0.40' = 400.00.
 systems trade (param): hvac -> 1.25 (baseline 808.88); near-miss WSR-56012-01 hvac but denied. systems market (param, cross purchase): Sierra Vista Ranch -> 1.30 (797.00). remaining coverage (param): 714 days from the settlement date -> 1.10 (851.00). maintenance record (param): 1 maintenance finding in 24 months -> 0.90 (929.00); the 4 within-tolerance findings are not maintenance findings. home scale (param, cross purchase): contract price 704,490 -> 1.20 (821.75). repeat-failure settlement (method): one accepted systems callback in 12 months -> scheduled 772.20 plus half the gap to 1,000.00 (scheduled alone: 772.20). Result 886.10; all-baseline 400.00.
No outcome stamp exists for any tier; all evidence is ledger rows, dates or other products' records.

6. WORLD
- customers (1) within the band (phone 9165550192, ssn 9047, ZIP 95747, surname S). purchase_agreements (1, closed Crestview, Sierra Vista Ranch SV-0563, contract 704,490.00, base 689,990 inside the Crestview band). homesite_reservations (1, Interior Homesite, Palmetto Shoals PS-0581, held, reserved 2026-09-28 on a 2026-09-15 prequalification letter, hold expiry 2026-10-12 = 14 days, funds 1,000.00) + homesite_events (1 reservation deposit, ach, RCPT-HS-58204, 2026-09-29, inside the 3 deposit days): feeds the active-buyer tier; nothing in the homesite product falls due before 2026-10-12.
- warranty_coverages (1, Preferred, start 2025-09-19): charges_due 0.00 = 48.00 - 48.00.
- warranty_events (30): walkthroughs (sixty-day 2025-11-07, HVAC check 2026-05-20, eleven-month 2026-08-20), drywall crack and its re-report (charged 48.00 = 100 x 0.80 x 1.00 x 1.00 x 0.75 x 0.80 on 2026-03-25, consistent with the extended rule that day; paid 2026-04-03), driveway crack and its re-report (uncharged), hvac item with repair, callback, callback approval and the 2026-09-08 inspection, the no-cooling emergency with dispatch, inspection and denial. Open obligations at frozen_time: exactly the two charges this task books; no missed appointment, no access window, no payout open.

7. PERSONA
Retired fire captain with a binder; volunteers only the surface goal and the story of the July repair, August recurrence and September 8 visit; identity, item number, the Sept 19 call, the driveway crack and the homesite hold only when asked; generic passive agreement if told other things must be recorded first; declines a repair visit; signs with exactly the values given; ends after the receipt; no extra asks.

8. STANDARD SOLUTION
find_customers(9165550192) -> verify(phone, 9047) -> find_warranty_coverages -> find_warranty_ledger -> find_purchase_agreements -> find_homesite_reservations -> find_homesite_ledger -> unlock+call assess_reinspection_charge_a99ab20e(coverage, WSR-55906-01, 25.20) -> unlock+call assess_emergency_dispatch_charge_91903470(coverage, WSR-56012-01, 48.99) -> unlock_user + (customer) accept_systems_item_cash_settlement_9ecd6f20(coverage, WSR-55841-01, 886.10).

9. VERIFICATION — _authoring/verify.py 1 --fill output: reinspection step 8 = 25.20 (factor baselines 31.50/20.16/36.00/28.00/31.50/50.40; all 100.00); dispatch step 10 = 48.99 (61.24/65.32/32.66/65.32/65.32/63.28; all 125.00); settlement step 12 = 886.10 after round 2 (808.88/797.00/851.00/929.00/821.75/772.20; all 400.00); skip edges: settlement 886.10 with and without step 10 (state gate), dispatch 48.99 with / 40.83 without step 8.
Gates (--task 1): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (13 actions, closure 35 = init 35); SOLVABILITY OK (10 base gates, 31 seed rows); COMPUTE OK (18 factors, 4 cross, 16 history rows, 47 branches); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK.
Revision log: (1) REPLAY mismatch: the homesite deposit row was read by no action (closure 34 vs 35) -> root cause: the active-buyer tier read only the reservation status -> change: the tier now requires a hold whose reservation deposit has been received (XCOUNT on homesite_events), rule/ladder/basis/inputs updated, find_homesite_ledger added as step 6, later steps shifted by one (computations, gold_actions, prior_step:10) -> REPLAY OK. (2) The dispatch rule first scoped itself to 'dispatches found homeowner-caused' while compute took the latest dispatch regardless -> rule restated as 'the most recent emergency dispatch ...; a dispatch whose claim item the inspection confirmed as a covered defect carries no dispatch charge' with a charge_due binding implementing it. (3) The dispatch prerequisite sentence was narrowed to re-measurements 'that the reinspection rules make chargeable' (a walkthrough the same day makes none).

10. SOLVABILITY CONTRACT vs GT
Steps 8 and 10 are state_due with intent from initial_state rows (the re-measurement, the dispatch) and stage preexisting_before_conversation; step 12 is on_request with discriminator 'take the cash for the upstairs air conditioning item' (verbatim) and stage performed_by_this_tool. policy_scope entries match the governing base policies exactly.

11. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT
From the rule prose, tool schemas and finder returns only: the settlement rule's 'not offered ... until' sentence -> the dispatch rule -> its 'fixed only after' sentence -> the reinspection rule; ledger shows both charges missing; 100 x .8 x 1.25 x .7 x .9 x .8 = 50.40, shared with one covered-work entry -> 25.20; 125 x .8 x .75 x 1.5 x .75 x .75 = 63.28125 x 12/15.5 -> 48.99; 1,000 x .4 x 1.25 x 1.3 x 1.1 x .9 x 1.2 = 772.20, one systems callback -> 886.10. Same objects, order and figures as gold.

12. MANUAL VALUES GATES (task 1 + difficulty)
Each hop is a real Calloway practice (a charge statement brought current before money is paid out; repeat non-warranty visits escalate the visit charge). Every write synchronous; no real-world wait. Rule/compute swept both ways; method factors change how a quantity is taken (visit sharing, response proration, repeat-failure settlement). Difficulty-level: 5 policies, 5 tools, 2 tasks, disjoint scopes, union = whole charter; each task has a user write, a multi-source factor and a cross-difficulty factor.

ROUND 2 REWORK (policy-task audit audits/policy_task/warranty_claims_service/, files _difficulty.md, 0.md, 1.md read in full)
Items bearing on this task:
- F6 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, prerequisite sentence gated 'paid', i.e. the later payout issue, not this policy's own result). Root cause: the sentence named payment, which in the charter is warranty_payout_issued. Change: the systems rule sentence and prerequisite[0].policy_source now read 'A systems settlement is not offered to the homeowner, and no cash-in-lieu payout is approved on it, until every emergency dispatch recorded on the coverage that the dispatch charge rules make chargeable carries its emergency dispatch charge.' The waited-on side is unchanged (one writer: the dispatch charge policy); the blocked side is now the policy's own result, the offer and the approved cash-in-lieu payout that the homeowner's acceptance records. prerequisite.effect, prerequisite_closure.edges[0] (policy_source, condition, flips_to_true_by), order_uniqueness (the false proof sentence about 'paid' replaced) and the persona's generic reaction ('before the settlement can go ahead') propagated. Re-run: order unique (chain), GT order reinspection -> dispatch -> accept unchanged.
- F7 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, remaining_coverage_anchor was a date substitution labelled method). Change: the anchor factor is removed from rule, compute (sys_approval_date, approval_age, anchor_shift deleted) and factors; the remaining-coverage multiplier now counts from the settlement date (714 days -> 365 to 729 tier, 1.10). A genuine method factor replaces it: repeat_failure_settlement_method, whose tiers change how the settlement is taken (two or more accepted systems callbacks in 12 months -> the cash-in-lieu maximum itself; exactly one -> scheduled plus half the gap; none -> scheduled), with the cap compared after that step. Evidence: systems approvals in 12 months (2026-06-17 original, 2026-08-15 callback_seq 1) less original approvals = 1. Still 6 factors (5 parameter + 1 honest method). Re-run (verify.py 1 --fill): settlement 886.10; factor baselines trade 808.88, market 797.00, remaining 851.00, maintenance 929.00, scale 821.75, repeat-failure method 772.20; all-baseline 400.00; every factor moves the result.
- F4 (latent: reinspection compute object broader than the rule). Change: rule restated so both faces have the same object: 'A reinspection charge is worked out for the most recent inspection recorded on the coverage that found a crack within tolerance ... linked to that inspection's claim item.' plus an explicit re-report test 'That inspection is the re-measurement of a re-reported item only when the coverage records at least two claim items filed in its defect category and at least two denials for within tolerance; where either count falls short, the inspection was of a first report and no reinspection charge is made.' Compute adds same_category_items, within_tolerance_denials and re_report (result 0.0 when false). This world: 2 concrete_flatwork items, 4 within-tolerance denials -> re-report, charge 25.20 unchanged. This also answers the audit observation that no record linked WSR-55906-01 to WSR-55620-01: the link is now a stated record test.
- F5 (latent: deposit not tied to the held reservation). Change: compute adds held_reservation = CFIELD('homesite','reservation_id', status='held') and hold_deposits counts reservation deposits with reservation_id = held_reservation; rule wording 'a homesite reservation on hold whose reservation deposit has been received' unchanged. A homesite reservation only reaches status held once its deposit is received (homesite lifecycle), so with several held reservations every one has a deposit and reading the first is equivalent. This world: one held reservation, its own deposit RCPT-HS-58204 -> 0.75, dispatch charge 48.99 unchanged.
- O2 (RND half-even vs docstring 'half up'): all five tool docstrings now say 'already rounded to the nearest cent'; no figure of either task sits on a half-cent tie.
- O3 (state_gate gate is a field name): kept; extended policies carry no eligibility list, so the field path warranty_events.charge_type is the record-visible state the sentence names. Recorded only.
Charter-level items closed in task 0's rework section: F1, F2, F3, O1, O4, O5. Gates re-run in full after the rework (see task 0 round-2 section).

ROUND 3 REWORK (audit revision_2 read in full; this task PASS there; F4-F7 left as closed)
- N2 (charter SOURCE-POLICY RED, latent, present since round 1: the dispatch edge `condition` was broader than its sentence). Root cause: the condition required a reinspection charge on every re-reported within-tolerance item, while the reinspection rules make none on a walkthrough day or when the re-report counts fall short. Change: warranty_ext_dispatch_charge.prerequisite[0].condition now reads 'Every within-tolerance inspection on the coverage that the reinspection rules make chargeable (counted as the re-measurement of a re-reported item by the claim-item and denial counts, and no walkthrough held on its date) is matched by ... reinspection_fee on that inspection's claim item; an inspection the rules leave uncharged needs no such row.' It is copied verbatim into prerequisite_closure.edges[1].condition. The finish/missed edge got the same treatment (N1; see task 0).
- O7 (latent: the re-report test is a count proxy that may differ from the base wording 'already denied within tolerance ... re-reported'). This difference is now declared rather than silent. The re-report sentence was moved next to the visit-charge sentence and states the proxy openly: 'The inspection a reinspection charge is worked out for counts as the re-measurement of a re-reported item only when the coverage records at least two claim items filed in that inspection's defect category and at least two denials for within tolerance, whichever claim items those denials concern; where either count falls short, the inspection counts as a first report and no reinspection charge is made.' The existing overwrite of the warranty_tolerances_and_exclusions sentence 'An item already denied within_tolerance that is re-reported and again measured within tolerance carries reinspection_fee_usd.' now names, as replaced_by, the two contiguous rule sentences (the re-report test and the visit-charge sentence). So the replacement of base's re-report condition is declared clause by clause; the parameter_schema description is base text and untouched. Basis quotes were re-pointed. On this world the earlier concrete item WSR-55620-01 was itself denied within tolerance, so the base wording and the proxy agree and the reinspection figure is unchanged.
- O8 (latent: CFIELD read only the first held reservation). Change: the active-buyer middle tier no longer ties the deposit to one reservation through a first-match read; both of its conditions are now customer-level and computed exactly. Rule: 'a homeowner with no such agreement but with a homesite reservation on hold and with a reservation deposit received on the homeowner's homesite ledger within the last 12 calendar months (dated later than the same calendar day 12 months before the assessment day) takes 0.75'. Compute: held_reservation removed; hold_deposits = XCOUNT(homesite_events, homesite_payment_received, reservation_deposit, within_months = new param deposit_window_months 12); homesite_hold = EXISTS held. Ladder, basis, cross_category note and inputs updated. No reservation-selection step remains, so there is no first-match residual. This world: reservation on hold, deposit 2026-09-29 within 12 months -> 0.75, figure unchanged; the eval step 6 necessity and the factor trace now describe the new tier.
- Re-run: --task 1 EXTENDED OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (expected, factor_sensitivity and baseline_result all recomputed equal). The full gate block is recorded in task 0's round-3 section.
user_scenario: You are Theodore Sandoval, Theo to most people, a retired fire captain who keeps every piece of paper about his house in a three-ring binder. You bought a new Calloway home in Sierra Vista Ranch, Roseville, and closed on it in September 2025. You speak slowly and patiently, a little dry, and you like to get things done in one call. You are calling about the air conditioning upstairs: the two upstairs bedrooms never cool properly. Calloway's HVAC contractor balanced the ducts in July, the problem came back in August, Calloway approved it again, and a technician came out on September 8 and agreed it is still not right, but nothing has been fixed since. You have decided you would rather take the cash for the upstairs air conditioning item than wait for another repair, because you want your own HVAC company to put in a zoning system. You want the cash settlement on that one upstairs air conditioning item, settled today, and you will sign the acceptance yourself; you are not asking for any other repair or appointment and you do not want anything else on the house changed. You open by saying who you are and that you would like to take the cash on the upstairs air conditioning problem instead of another repair. When the agent asks how to find you, give your phone number, 9165550192. To confirm your identity give the last four of your Social Security number, 9047; if one more item is needed, your ZIP code is 95747 and your email is theo.sandoval@yahoo.com. If the agent asks which item it is, read it from your binder: the upstairs air conditioning is item WSR-55841-01. Only if the agent asks about the emergency call on September 19, say the technician found the return-air filter clogged and the condensate switch tripped, and that one was on you. Only if the agent asks about the driveway crack, say they measured it again on September 8 and told you it is still within tolerance, and you have accepted that. Only if the agent asks whether you have any other business with Calloway, say you put a hold on a homesite in Palmetto Shoals, near your daughter in Bluffton, at the end of September. You do not know how Calloway prices settlements or fees, you have no figure in mind and you never suggest one. If the agent explains that other things have to be recorded on your account before the settlement can go ahead, you say that is fine, the rules are the rules, and tell them to go ahead; you do not ask to pay anything on this call and you do not dispute anything. If the agent offers another repair visit instead, decline and repeat that you would rather have the cash. When the agent tells you the settlement amount and hands you the acceptance, sign it yourself using exactly the coverage reference number, item number and amount the agent gives you. Once it shows as recorded, thank the agent and end the call without asking for anything else.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's homeowner profile from the phone number he gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write is keyed by the customer reference number this lookup returns.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm the caller is Theodore Sandoval with two matching items (phone and last four of the SSN).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No account detail may be discussed and no charge or settlement recorded before identity passes the 2-item threshold.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read his HomeCare 2-3-10 Preferred coverage: coverage reference number, coverage start 2025-09-19, systems end date 2028-09-18 and the purchase agreement of the home.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The program sets the reinspection fee, the emergency dispatch fee and response hours, the repair target days and the cash-in-lieu maximum; the start date feeds the settling-period and first-period multipliers; the systems end date feeds the remaining-coverage multiplier; the coverage id is the target of all three writes.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the warranty history: the re-reported driveway crack WSR-55906-01 re-measured within tolerance on 2026-09-08 with no reinspection charge, the earlier drywall reinspection charge WCH-55391, the no-cooling emergency dispatch of 2026-09-19 on WSR-56012-01 (maintenance finding, no dispatch charge), the hvac item WSR-55841-01 with its callback approval of 2026-08-15 and the 2026-09-08 defect-confirming inspection.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: This read discovers both unmet prerequisites (the systems-settlement rule says it 'is not offered to the homeowner, and no cash-in-lieu payout is approved on it, until every emergency dispatch ... that the dispatch charge rules make chargeable carries its emergency dispatch charge'; the dispatch-charge rule says it 'is fixed only after every re-reported item that a re-measurement again found within tolerance and that the reinspection rules make chargeable carries its reinspection charge') and supplies every history row the eighteen factors rest on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the home's purchase agreement: community Sierra Vista Ranch, contract price 704,490.00, closed; and confirm no other agreement is under construction or closing scheduled.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Community decides the soil-movement and systems market multipliers; contract price decides the home-scale multiplier; the absence of another open agreement keeps the active-buyer multiplier off its top tier (cross-difficulty evidence).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read his Palmetto Shoals homesite reservation PS-0581, status held.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A homesite reservation on hold puts the active-buyer multiplier of the dispatch charge on its 0.75 tier (cross-difficulty evidence).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Palmetto Shoals reservation ledger: the 1,000.00 reservation deposit received 2026-09-29 (receipt RCPT-HS-58204).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The active-buyer multiplier's 0.75 tier needs a homesite reservation on hold together with a reservation deposit received on the homeowner's homesite ledger within the last 12 calendar months; this deposit row (2026-09-29) is that evidence (cross-difficulty ledger read).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the reinspection charge tool named by the reinspection charge rule.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the leaf prerequisite; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Book the reinspection charge for the 2026-09-08 within-tolerance re-measurement of the re-reported driveway crack WSR-55906-01.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Leaf problem of the tree: the dispatch charge waits on it and counts it among the non-warranty visit charges.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.coverage_id: Value: 1af4f065-344e-43c1-b1bd-e22d6dedf9df. Basis: tool docstring 'coverage_id: Id class — the reference number of the homeowner's warranty coverage on the home'; find_warranty_coverages returns exactly one coverage for Theodore.
